title: Empellón

reviews.review: I've been here twice and this place is fantastic. The food is unmatched, especially the wagyu tacos, which, despite being pricey, are life-changing. Their salsa sampler is also so fun and unique, and provides such a diverse selection of salsas to try. The waiters are super kind and great about making recommendations, and even comped a dessert for us the first time I was here just because they loosely knew the person I was with. The space is also beautiful, especially the upper level. Super romantic, great lighting, and a perfect date night spot.

Had a business lunch here and was thoroughly disappointed. The space is nice and service is attentive. However, the room was very chilly and the food was below average. I ordered the pastrami taco which sounded interesting yet turned out to be a huge hunk of meat on top of a very thin tortilla. Nothing else is served on the side to make this an edible dish. My colleagues also struggled eating their "tacos". It is a truly poor representation of tacos all around. The guac was ok. Skip this.

I met a friend here for dinner recently, as she raved about the food. On the whole, everything tasted good, but there wasn't anything SO sensational that I'll be in a hurry to return. It tends to be on the noisier side, but due to the weather, I think it could've been worse. Food arrives quickly, so I'll give them credit on that. There was a mishap that I think could have been handled better, but more on that in a minute. Here's an overview of what we ordered:

Guacamole ($24): The guacamole itself isn't a particularly large portion, but I don't think anyone orders it for that really. It's the seven salsas in mini ramekins, ranging from mild to hot, that really makes this worth ordering. 

Pastrami Tacos ($28): This piqued my interest. We enjoyed this very much, but I would say it tastes exactly as it sounds. Imagine you heated up some Trader Joe's pastrami, placed it on a corn tortilla, added a little sauerkraut and mustard seeds, you would have precisely the same output. Worth noting, tacos are served two to a platter.

Aromatic Beef Short Ribs ($44): Again, tasty, but not epic. Tasted similar to what I make in my slow cooker at home. I've had incredible short ribs elsewhere, but this was just fine. Not special, not bad by any means. Not sure the price is justified.

Sweet Corn ($15): A relatively small-medium bowl of corn, it's tasty but not amazing. I actually couldn't tell there was chorizo in it. Good, but like everything else, nothing to write home about.

Roasted Shishito Peppers ($15): Very generous portion on this one. Loads of peppers on a plate. They're prepared about as well as you'd expect.

¿Por Que No?  Margarita ($20): Tasted good. No complaints. Just your average margarita on the rocks with a slice of pineapple & salted rim.

I probably wouldn't have bothered with a review if that was all there was to the experience, but here's why I docked an extra star: while eating our mains, a girl was trying to get into the booth seat for her table next to my friend. Since they crunch the tables so close together, this very thin girl in her 20s struggled to get through without incident, and so she accidentally knocked over the glass carafe of water on our table and it shattered everywhere. 

She was absolutely mortified - I really felt for her. She kept apologizing as we hurried to control the water, offering to replace our drinks as we did, and we just kept telling her it's okay. My friend's skirt was soaked with water, as was her seat, glass all over our short ribs, corn, guacamole + salsas, her martini, our water glasses, and the shishito peppers.  Fortunately, I had just finished my margarita, and wasn't planning on ordering another one. The bus boy made a concerted attempt to clean up the glass and water, although my friend's seat was still wet and glass was still in our food and on the table, floor, etc. I eventually gave my friend my napkin so she could sit, which was unfortunately not replaced. 

A little while later, the bus boy asked if we'd like another drink (and I'm pretty sure he meant, would we like to pay for more drinks). I declined because I had just finished, but pointed out my friend's half-full martini had floating glass in it. He asked her if she still wanted it, but I think that was due to a language barrier. Eventually our server came around with replacement drinks for my friend and I, and said it was courtesy of our neighbor. I felt sort of bad because I wasn't planning on drinking anymore, and these drinks had to set this early 20-something year old girl back an extra $50 on top of her meal, for what was absolutely an accident, not completely unprovoked by tight spacing. I felt the classy thing to do would be for the restaurant to replace my friend's drink and the affected food, but that didn't seem to occur to them. 

After we pointed out to our waiter that we weren't comfortable eating the food with glass shards in it, they asked if we just wanted them to take it away / call it done, or pack it up. Which is kind of crazy because we weren't even half-way through with the $44 short ribs, and hadn't yet touched the $15 peppers. But no, not interested in packing up food with sharp glass in it. Would kind of prefer they just replaced the dishes? Ultimately, they let us weigh whether we wanted to risk our lives with glass for a couple of minutes before finally stepping in and replacing our short ribs and shishito peppers. Unfortunately they didn't think to do the same with the corn, guac, or even our water glasses. At one point, I got so thirsty, I decided to risk it and try to filter out glass with my teeth just so I could drink some water. I gave up on the rest.

All of that aside, it was a fine time and everyone was polite. Naturally, it wasn't the restaurant's fault that the girl broke the carafe - that was an accident. But the tight squeeze probably was, and it's a little disappointing that they were so quick to profit off this poor girl yet hesitated to take away the glass.

When visiting NYC a few years ago, we visited a sister restaurant so we decided we wanted to try the original one while in town. We started the meal with the guacamole which comes with seven different salsas! So fun and tasty! Our favorite salsa was the chile de arbol and salsa verde. Guacamole was excellent. We shared the pastrami tacos and BLT sopes as our mains. The pastrami was delicious and the sopes were clever. We had the side of Brussel sprouts which were amazing. The service was OK. The waiter was not terribly attentive but was pleasant. The expediters and bus staff were very attentive and helpful. The restaurant is decorated very nicely, fun environment. We would certainly go back.

Great spot if you are looking for some fushion style Mexican food. Fantastic margaritas. Highly suggest the quac and quesadillas (something I never would recommend but they were fantastic). 
Service is great, but they do get crowded. If you go during happy hour times I suggest going early. 

Strongly suggest the Madison location over the upper west side. UWS is a "to go" so although the food is still good, it comes in aluminum tins over the real dishes (deal breaker for me!). But highly suggest the Madison Ave spot
Food was very tasty, amazing service (nice servers) and the ambience was great. Also the bathrooms were very nice and clean.

This was my first time here, and I will be going back many more times. We ate at the bar. The spicy cucumber margarita is delicious. I highly recommend it. I ordered the cheeseburger tacos, the grilled fish tacos, and my husband and I shared the guacamole and salsa flight.
I can't say enough about their food. 
It's an upscale, Mexican dining experience. Before we left, I had to ask the manager how they kept their corn tortillas so soft and so fresh without tearing. It's truly an art.

What an experience. Cocktails are great. Service is great. Order many different tapas and share. Pricy but with it. 
Beautiful place - nice to sit upstairs tables.

Don't bother having a reservation! We had to wait in the bar area for over 30min.

Food was just okay, not worth the wait and inconvenience.

I probably had a few too many "mother of dragons" but this place is a blast. 

They start you with a salsa sampler with not one, not two, not three, but seven different salsas.  I'm a real sauce aficionado so this was exciting for me.  

Our group ordered family style so we got to try a bit of everything.  Tacos were great (would say a bit Westernized, not in a negative way).  Real star of the show was the rib-steak fajita.  

Our server, Mateo was wonderful as well!

Met a friend here for an early dinner. The outdoor bar was packed and the indoor bar was busy.  The restaurant is modern looking and very echoic.  We were seated upstairs and it was a lot quieter. The staff were very nice. Cocktails were very good. Extra credit for having an overproof gin. The food was simply fabulous.  We shared the guacamole with 7 salsas- excellent!  The chips were off the charts. I was blown away by their crab nachos.  We also had excellent fish tempura tacos and astonishingly good pastrami tacos. The shishito peppers were really good too. It's easy to spend a lot of money here.  There were a lot of specials, all expensive. I couldn't do $80 steak fajitas either. The $26 hot dog at Mischa now makes sense. We were too full to try the avocado ice cream. 

I came to this restaurant expecting to be disappointed or ripped off.  We had a fabulous meal. I loved sharing a bunch of small plates.

Empellon was a big disappointment as the food and service didn't live up to the potential. What could have been bold or interesting flavors were overall quite bland. The Mitake Mushroom Tacos were gummy and lacked acid.  The fish tacos were essentially what you could make at home. The aromatic beef short ribs smelled amazing but lacked any seasoning. Even their signature margarita tasted store bought. The complexity of the seven salsas (which outshined the guacamole) was missing from everything else. As for service, our waiter was very helpful in recommending the right amount of food, but the service was rushed. The tacos came out mere seconds after the guac and salsa and the entries came out while we were still finishing the tacos As the server waited for us to make room on the table.  All this for an early reservation on a Friday eve with many tables open. My two companions got up to use the bathroom at the end of the meal and that's when the server decided to bring over an ice cream dessert ball "thank yous" instead of waiting until they returned. All in all, a big miss.

Have heard amazing things about this restaurant and came here for dinner last week and was extremely disappointed. 

We ordered a bunch of different things and there wasn't one that l would recommend. The steak lacked seasoning, and the salsa covering the bone marrow overpowered its flavor completely. The tuna tartare was not fresh and the sweet potato side seemed like was just thrown together and heated up. The server was suggesting us to order more and there was just way too much food on the table (probably trying to make more tips) 

Would not recommend!

I had the Chicken and beef. These are genuinely some of the worst tacos I have ever had. First of all its ground chicken and ground beef. I think they literally went to Costco, bought the cheapest meat they offer, threw it in a pot  and called it taco meat. the fact this place costs so much should be illegal.

I was expecting a lot. The only good thing about dining here was being with my coworkers. The server we had was outstanding. Food presentation was not what I was expecting. Fish tacos were blah, drinks were just ok. Nachos were fresh, guacamole was just ok. There was a blonde server/hostess who was just rude and not friendly or professional at all.  Had very high hopes for this restaurant. Will not go back. Can get better drinks at Rosa Mexicano. Better guacamole at Besitos in West Islip or Huntington. Ambiance was just OK. I think if you're going to work in food industry, especially at a restaurant, the service shoul be great. This place was no where near great. I'm being nice by giving them 1 star!  Save yourself and go where you feel welcomed and treated better.  Go to Rosa Mexicano!
Service and decor were impeccable, plating was gorgeous, food tasted good and was imaginative but portions were small for the price.

Went there for a business dinner.  I had been there for lunch so was excited to try them for  dinner 

The menu was set so we started with the 7 sauces and chips.  Nice start. 

The tuna tartare on a bed of something was ok.  Fair start but out of place with the cuisine.  The cabbage salad was refreshing and a good in between

The tacos were hard shell beef of some sort and the soft ones fried fish.  I tried neither so cannot comment. The beef was commented on as being ok with a lot of fat.  The fish was also commented as ok. 

The entree was the skirt steak and the steamed halibut.  The halibut was good but not very tasty other than the salt. Skirt steak was good and the rub in it worked to give it flavor.  

Dessert was the ice cream sandwich which I did not try. 

Overall it was noisy and service was good.
Went in without reservation and were pleasantly surprised. Service was great, food was tasteful and the dining room was pretty cool. No complaints here. We will be back!

The seating on the ground floor was unreasonably tight with my seat frequently getting kicked and me making physical contact with waitstaff. The crowd being largely corporate people who don't want to splurge on more expensive restaurants does detract from what I would otherwise brand a hip atmosphere.

The menu is small but focused. Every dish was excellent. Two tacos at these prices ($20s and $30s) hurts but the pastrami tacos were great. Queso fundido was indeed a fun take, and the carnitas dish was deeply satisfying. Even the tortillas were notable. A great Mexican spot that somehow manages to fly a bit under the radar.
Food was not worth the price.  Was shocked that Pete Wells recommended this spot.  Service was spotty.  Better Spanish restaurants to go to in this town.
Without a doubt Alex stupaka desserts shine brightly here. He is truly a master of the sandbaggery as you can see with his tacos. Yet again I suggest going here for the desserts first and foremost.

Came in for dinner with a visiting friend on a Saturday who is obsessed with the cookbook. Midtown Corporate dinner spot so it was unsurprisingly pretty empty for a Saturday night. The staff was extremely attentive and helpful. We ordered the crab nachos, smoked black cod, fish tempura, picadillo taco and the skirt steak. The apps were pretty good and we were pretty full from the nachos and black cod alone. I wouldn't skimp on the apps. To be honest, the tacos were unmemorable and pretty meh. The steak was pretty solid but we were pretty full by the time they came around. The drinks were very good. The saffron margarita is not to be missed. The restaurant is beautiful though, I love the clay art pieces they have on the first floor -both beautiful and grotesque. I would probably swing by again if I had the corporate card and was struggling to snag a reservation in midtown to impress but I would definitely not be visiting on my own dime.

This place was on my list for a while so I got to say I was underwhelmed and sadly so .
The guac is good and those salsas (7 of them) are excellent to dip in .
The lobster taco was fantastic, the mushrooms ones were very good . 
The entrees .... Well the halibut was fair but on the dry side and the special of the day short ribs was just an ok red meat . Pretty disappointing entrees.
At least at the final the desert - " The Avocado" was
Spectacular!!! What a genius idea , one of the best photogenic (or as they say instagramble) desert that actually delivers.
Fantastic service and very nice (excellent rare acoustically) and friendly space .

I came to the midtown location for my birthday dinner and it was all around an excellent experience. They were able to accommodate my large group of 14 people with the pre-fixe menu and the service was superb. Every course was delicious and the drinks were excellent. They paid special attention to my friend with food allergies and made sure she had alternative options for each course. We had a time restraint because we were seeing a show and the team was sure to keep things rolling per my request. While the tacos and steak were fan-favorites, I think the avocado key lime dessert took the cake for most impressive dish. 

It can be very hard to find a place in NYC to host a large group, especially during the holiday season, so I could not recommend Empellon more!

We ran through a Yelp list of the best Mexican restaurants in NYC recently, and Empellon didn't show up among the first 150. While we haven't tried many of those restaurants, we have been here and believe it should rank much higher. The cuisine is Mexican-inspired, as the hosts say, but it is imaginative and well done, and we thought the service was especially sharp. 

The highlight? Well, the margaritas were good-sized and delicious, and the specialty margaritas featuring some very high-end tequilas were really outstanding. And we loved the fresh guacamole and the "seven salsas,"a small dish a serving of these treats arranged from mild to spicy which made devouring them something of an adventure. Excellent. The steak fajitas were prepared to our liking -- a little less than medium -- and while we liked the lobster tacos (?), the lobster bits turned out a bit chewy. Far better was the tuna tartare, an item we hadn't expected at this restaurant. 

The restaurant has some tasty and fancy desserts, but we opted for -- wait for it -- the chocolate ice cream sandwich! Yep, ultra-simple and ultra-yummy, a perfect finish to the meal for us and highly recommended. 

A good restaurant, then, if a bit on the noisy side when crowded. We sat in the large upstairs section where noise levels were better than in the bar and the seating areas below. As noted, the service was excellent. The prices here are, let's be honest, on the high side. It's not a Taco Bell, rather a destination for an upscale Mexican night out.

First customer service note: when the person who made the reservation (for 2) arrives on time and wants to be seated, it's highly aggravating and obnoxious to be told you have to stand around and wait for "the rest of your party" .... Really off putting and leaving me already sorry I considered dropping any money here. Am hoping that better service will follow if and when I get my table. Not a good start.

This Mexican restaurant was over priced. When you walk in the ambiance says I'm fancy, and about to be overpriced. The cost was just not worth it. The food was equivalent to a fancy Taco Bell. I appreciated our mock tails came in fancy glasses. The staff was friendly and attentive.

Crab nachos was well prepared. Served well as an appetizer. It wasn't to overfilling but perfectly paired with the other ingredients.

The fish tempura tacos were good nothing too amazing that made them stick out to me. They tasted good it was not overly seasoned.

The stone free drink was good, it had a taste similar to skittles. It was good but I prob wouldn't have it again as skittles taste isn't that appealing to me.


Service was amazing, they have coat check, attentive hostesses , and servers .

Ambiance was more on the upscale.

Came here with work friends for the pre fix lunch menu.  The food was good but nothing mind blowing.  Their signature dessert, ice cream shaped as an avocado looked very realistic, but the flavor didn't match up.  Worth trying but wouldn't order again.

Here, innovation is only surpassed by amazing flavor. After seeing what a viral sensation the avocado dessert had become, we made a beeline over there as soon as we could.

The hosts were welcoming, even though we were within 45 minutes of close. This might sound like something you'd expect, but that's not always the case.

Because we were a little bit more peckish than dessert can satisfy, we tried the mushroom tacos first. They are the best soft mushroom tacos I've ever had.

Then, for the avocado dessert. Do yourself a favor, and Google this. There are food writers that will do much better job describing it than I will. I'll simply call it a flavor fiesta. 

Ok that sounds really dumb, but I'm going with it because I'm that kind of person. 

Additionally, this place does an amazing job of deadening, the sounds of a restaurant. We had no trouble having an easy-going conversation without competing against the din of clacking plates and ongoing discussion. Just a great environment to have a meal in.

After a full day of sightseeing and shopping, i stopped by Empellon for a much needed cocktail. They weren't too busy at 5 PM so I was able to grab a seat at the bar, but by 6 PM the bar was packed with people grabbing a drink after work and the restaurant was filling up quickly too. It's a very clean facility with lots of seating, including a huge upstairs area. The bartenders were all super friendly. I ordered a Spicy cucumber margarita, which as a hint of mezcal, so refreshing! The food looked good too.
This is potentially the worst food I've had in my life. I'm not kidding. Im so surprised i wasn't puking that night.

Like many before me, I came to Empellon primarily for the dessert and didn't give too much advance thought to the rest of the menu, but I ended up liking everything I tried. 

The guacamole was pretty standard in terms of the actual guac, but the addition of the "seven salsas", which sounds vaguely mythic, turns the act of eating an appetizer into an event. Everyone tries all of them at least once and comments on their favorites, least favorites, etc. They range in order from least spicy to spiciest. I liked them all, but the most memorable to me was a creamy, smoky dip. 

I also ordered the maitake mushroom tacos, which were served on a soft tortilla and topped with quesillo and cilantro. The mushrooms were drenched in a delicious piquant sauce; I loved each savory bite. My favorite part of the taco might've actually been the soft, immensely chewy, slightly oily tortilla. 

Empellon is also known for its margaritas, and I couldn't resist trying the saffron-infused version, which came with a saffron salt rim. The saffron flavor wasn't too strong or subtle and the drink was obviously made with high-quality ingredients. For some reason, the drink didn't totally blow me away; I was more of a fan of the spicy cucumber margarita that my friend ordered. Obviously go for this if you're a big saffron fan.

Last but certainty not least, we ordered the famed avocado dessert, which - as you've probably heard - looks exactly like an avocado but remarkably tastes like a silky key lime pie custard. The "salt" is super citrusy raspado (Mexican shaved ice). It's just a really impressive dessert. Tastes great, but surely what makes the dish unique its masterful, playful construction. 

Empellon is in the heart of midtown (53rd off of Madison), which can always feel like a questionable choice for a Saturday night meal, but honestly, the crowd was lively, and there's something to be said for the almost grandiose feel afforded to the restaurant by the spacious, bi-level, interior. I was happy to be there.

Fun, vibrant, stylish atmosphere, with excellent food and cocktails. The staff really know their cuisine; the menu offers really interesting choices and the creative versions of carrot salad and flan I  had were robust and bright.

Came here for dessert after finding out earlier during the day that the restaurant has some very unique desserts. We tried the Avocado and the Corn Ice-Cream Taco. Both were very good. I really liked the way the Avocado tasted. The lime flavor wasn't too strong and went perfectly with the eucalyptus yogurt.
What a beautiful restaurant! With exceptional service. The food is totally different and creative. Love everything here,especially their salsas...
Exceptional mexican food in NYC. Would definitely go back - loved the drinks, guac was special and the fish tacos!!

Amazing, amazing, amazing! The food and service were top-notch.  A friend and I shared a salad, 2 mains, and a dessert.  The cabbage salad was bright with a great bite. I loved everything about the pastrami tacos. The bean sauce with the steamed halibut is so good that I would drink it from a cup.  The perfect end to the meal was the Avacado lime raspado. It was light and perfectly paired with lime shaved ice.  So good.

Let's start at the end and work backwards: the avocado dessert is WORTH THE HYPE. I'd come here just for this. It was one of the most delicious things I've ever had. I'm not a dessert person and it was the perfect level of sweetness for me. Not to mention it's just fun and instagram worthy.

I also got the chips and seven salsas. I enjoyed all of the salsas but I was surprised at how much I enjoyed the lowest level one with cashews. The habanero took me by surprise but as a heat lover it was tolerable. I think my favorite was mezcal or the chipotle one. The guac was also very good.

Margs: I tried two. The pineapple one and the cucumber spicy one. I liked the cucumber one more although most of the heat came from the garnish on the rim.

We shared chips with the different salsas and it was a great variety of choices.   They give you a little spoon with each salsa so no need to dip.  We both had the fish tacos and they were perfectly cooked, a little crispy and extremely tender.   Two was plenty.  We split the avocado mousse dessert.   It's interesting and subtle.   Service was superb.   They didn't rush us at all even though the restaurant was full.
The food was amazing. Omg the tuna tartare was  it was busy when I went so I understand it may have been hard for the server to be more attentive.

This place was suggested by our concierge at our hotel and he sure was right! It's great food and incredible customer service starting with the wonderful host who greeted us. Simply  wonderful. We had the steak tacos and wow is all I can say! Our sides were delicious. We ordered Brussels sprouts and sweet potatoes. If you'd like Mexican cuisine, don't pass this place up!
Food and service were superb.  Loved the black cod and el pastor.   Also the avacadp dessert was amazing.

The crab nachos with uni were very good but everything else was mediocre at best. We came in a large group of 8 and here's what we ordered (family style):

- Chips and guacamole and 7 salsas for $22 (3/10): The chips weren't great (tasted a little stale) and the guacamole was unremarkable. Didn't love the salsas and they came in these super tiny cups which meant you couldn't dip your chips in them. 
- Crab nachos with uni (9/10): These were fantastic. Maybe the only good thing we ordered, except maybe also the Brussel sprouts. 
- Tacos: the lobster tacos and fish tempura tacos weren't bad but the pastrami was terrible. Others tried the Maitake mushrooms taco and didn't like it. 
- Salads (5/10): the salads aren't really salads....wish we were warned that ahead of time. The chopped cabbage vaguely resembled a salad and was decently refreshing but the English peas salad in no way resembled a salad (see photos). That said, it was decently refreshing. 
- Steamed halibut (2/10): I took one bite and couldn't have anymore. It was over cooked and had 0 flavor. And it was a tiny piece yet costed $45.
- Rib steak fajitas (6/10): This wasn't bad, relatively speaking. 
- Brussel sprouts with spicy almonds (8/10): These were actually pretty good. 
- avocado dessert (6/10): Not bad but not sure what all the hype was for. I liked the creamy texture and it was something new to try but definitely nothing to write home about and I couldn't have more than a few bites.

Service was also weird. They kept taking stuff away when we weren't done with them. The waitress even took my margarita when I wasn't done so I told her I was still working on it, then she put it back down then weirdly changed her mind and picked it back up and took it away. Bizarre.

Do not recommend coming here.

When it comes to presentation and style, Empellón delivers! The spacious atmosphere of this flagship restaurant entices friends, partners, and coworkers alike to dine in and imbibe with food & drinks that don't disappoint. My friend and I sat upstairs--and even with a large gathering of what appeared to be a group of coworkers sitting near us, our space felt respected.

The only downside is that the food portions overall could be bigger for the prices. In other words, you're definitely paying for the environment when you dine here. (I do love the view of the restaurant's decor & design from the stairs!) My friend and I shared the smoked black cod, roasted shishito peppers, and skirt steak. My favorite of the three was the smoked black cod with a potato-chorizo vinaigrette--a delicious combo I haven't tried before. The shishito peppers were actually a good size--but for $17, that felt like a stretch to me. As for the skirt steak, the six pieces wouldn't suffice as a stand-alone meal for many individuals (perhaps Empellón expects everyone to order appetizers)--and the onions seemed to overpower the dish. We could have ordered more food but didn't necessarily feel in the mood to spend more. I'd say I wouldn't come here often because of the portion-to-price ratio, but it's still a nice place to hit up occasionally!

Such a great twist on the classics! Everything was delicious and fresh and the staff was professional and accommodating. It was nice that they did not rush us out even though the restaurant was busy. 

We ordered guac and the 7 salsas to start, which was great and there's a spice level for everyone. We also had the cabbage salad, the lobster bisque, the fish tacos, the mushroom tacos and the steak tacos. For dessert we tried sherbert and the avocado mousse, which I think I would skip next time. Overall this is a great spot in midtown for lunch and would try for dinner!

Everything here is just ok. Nothing great, nothing terrible. For the price, we expected a lot better. First off, the margaritas are not good. They taste like they use a cheap mix vs. fresh ingredients. Also, they do not know how to make a spicy drink; we ordered several versions and asked for extra spicy ones, which turned out incredibly mild. 

In terms of food, the guacamole and dips is a fun idea, but the salsas were just mediocre. Nothing really blew us away. One even tasted like ketchup, and not in a good way. I would bypass the tacos overall, except for the fish taco, which was the best thing we had that night. The mushroom taco tasted like tomato sauce with little flavor, and the pastrami taco needed something, so we added the mustard salsa from the dips which made it decent.

The steak fajita is a platter of ribeye with very little that's interesting or new.

In addition to disappointing food, the service was very sporadic. At one point, I waited over 30 minutes for my drink, and we were finished with dinner when I finally got it which was frustrating.

Just overall a disappointment, especially for my birthday dinner. I will not return it and would not recommend it.

Let me start by saying this place has good food. We got shishito peppers as an appetizer, beef picadillo tacos and jumbo tiger pawns fajitas and it was all tasty; so was the wine we ordered, though I'm not sure which one it was, since I wasn't the one who ordered it. We were not big fans of avocado desert, but that's a personal preference. The place is decorated nice enough, but I'm not sure about the ambiance. It's like they couldn't decide which direction to take it. There are people who are dressed up and equally those who are in more casual attire. The tables are very close together and the music is loud so it's hard to hear your companion. However, they did play some good, modern music which I enjoyed. I just feel like it should either be a casual place to grab lunch/dinner or a 'fancy, nice restaurant' and this was kind of neither here, nor there. Service was great! Everyone  who helped us, were very nice. Pretty good experience overall.

This place used to be known for its great tacos. Well, we there for lunch and the two (!! - not three) tacos we got were abysmal. And cost $24. That's not even the worst part. The worst part is that I ended up with absolutely terrible food poisoning after visiting the restaurant and I have no doubt in my mind that it was caused by the $33 lobster salad I ate.

The service was not good either, they kept on asking whether they can collect the plates while we were still eating our tiny portions.

The ambiance is also very 'corporate like' and you will  hear everything the table next to you is saying. Therefore, not a great place for a business lunch either.

I will never visit this restaurant again and it's a shame it's gone so much downhill in such a short time.

I would definitely come back here. It's beautifully decorated. We sat upstairs; it was easy to carry a conversation without being distracted.

Food recommendations: 
Guacamole with seven salsas, Smoked black cod, and pastrami tacos were all amazing. Seven salsas are arranged from least to most spicy. The first one is smokey creamy, and it's my favorite. My friends love the spiciest one. The desert avocado is a nice refreshing desert.

I would come back here. Some things I loved - some thing that could change/be improved.

We came in an ordered ~all~ the appetizers:

- Guacamole SEVEN SALSAS
- Crab Nachos SEA URCHIN "QUESO"
- Tuna Tartare SUNFLOWER SEEDS, CHILE ASH CURED BONITO
- Smoked Black Cod POTATO-CHORIZO VINAIGRETTE
- Queso Fundido STEAK TARTARE
- Roasted Shishito Peppers LIME VINAIGRETTE

*What I LOVED (and why):
- Guacamole SEVEN SALSAS (delicious assortment of salsas and makes food fun in the sense that it's an activity; all the salsas and guacamole were delicious. Chips were great, too!)
- Crab Nachos SEA URCHIN "QUESO" (I love nachos - so this was a great dish that was also very hearty and well spiced.)
- Roasted Shishito Peppers LIME VINAIGRETTE (very impressed with this - extremely well flavored and was able to compete with the other dishes.)

*What I won't order again (and why):
- Tuna Tartare SUNFLOWER SEEDS, CHILE ASH CURED BONITO (very bland, and no where near the same flavoring and spicing as the other dishes.)
- Smoked Black Cod POTATO-CHORIZO VINAIGRETTE (what a disappointment-- little to no taste and the sauce was so overbearing that I either only tasted the sauce or the cod which was underwhelming.)
- Queso Fundido STEAK TARTARE (nope, not a fan. Steak tartare should be what it is. This was steak tartare minced onto a block of cheese and just ruined the steak.)

On a Tuesday night, it was pretty loud. I don't mind. But be prepared if you're trying to have a one-on-one convo with the person in front of you sitting on the other side of the table it might be a challenge (at least for downstairs).

In general, I had a mixed impression and experience with the waiting staff. They were very sweet but also a bit pushy.

Would come back again - just with a better idea of what I want!

I've been to Empellon several times.  I've returned many times, because I thought it was a great place.   However, their management staff has little respect for their returning customers.  A simple experience can spoil every last good experience I've had.   Unfortunately, that's what happened.. I've visited this location with my work colleagues at

The was a pretty amazingly good meal.  The guacamole flight was  worth price of admission.  Several different salsa's some hot some not.  A wonderful array of different flavors.   The guacamole was fresh and simple preparation of perfect avocado.  The chips were actually fried corn tortillas which were excellent.   I had the skirt steak. It was tender and perfectly cooked and even though rare it came to the table still warm. Another excellent salsa. It was accompanied by a salad of sautéed onions (scallions and shallots at least).  We also had the dish tacos which were full with a very light batter almost tempera like .  The portion was ample.  The classic margaritas were well made.  

The service was nicely paced, efficient and friendly. We  had an excellent post dinner conversation the management and how much we enjoyed the meal. 

The restaurant is hard hence the ambiance can be  loud.  It was a thoroughly enjoyable evening

Delicious. A wide array of choices for herbivores and omnivores alike. Ordered through the $45 lunch prefix and got the cauliflower soup (amazing), the Mushroom tacos (very good,) and the chocolate ice cream sandwich (good!) Definitely will be back.

Rare high end Mexican food place near my home. I really enjoy their cocktails and guac. I always go back for their avocado dessert. The only sad thing is that their portions are often too big for me so theres very few dishes i could order each time i go.
When in midtown east go to this restaurant for the lunch prix fix and supplement with the lobster salad and avocado dessert.

Food, cocktails, service, & atmosphere was great.  I had the spicy cucumber margarita.  It was so delicious..in fact I had 2 of them. The Seven Salsas are a must have & their homemade chips are amazing.  Also had the Hamachi Tartare, Red & Green Chorizo, Skirt Steak Taco, & Fish Tempura Taco.  All were so good.  I highly recommend Empellon, & will definitely be back!!!

I made two trips to Empellon before writing this review. I love Mexican food, and will usually have tacos at low key places but I was pretty happy about a more up-scale experience with Mexican food. The ambience is lovely. There are two floors. There is an elevator available as well for those who cannot take the stairs. 

In the first visit, we ordered guacamole, tacos and the avocado dessert. In the second visit we got the crab nachos, tuna tartare and seared halibut. 

Based on the first visit I would have rated this place 4/5. The guacamole is good and it comes with an array of sauces arranged from mildest to hottest. I enjoyed the experience of trying them all out. The tacos left a bit more to be desired. It's hard to explain why...maybe they needed more filling..? The ratio of the meat to the tortilla seemed a bit off. The avocado dessert is a nice summery dessert. I would describe it as a key lime yogurt mousse. I felt like it needed something else, like a cookie or cake base or something. The service was okay. 

My next trip is what bumped Empellon up to 5 stars. I absolutely loved the crab nachos. They were so flavorful. I did notice a review about dry nachos so I hesitated to order them, but the ones I got were really well made with lots of topping. I enjoyed the tuna tartare a lot. The halibut, white mild flavored for a Mexican meal was cooked so well that I had to give it a 5/5. The dessert this time was also a lot better. I got the coconut mousse. The pleasant surprise was that it was a chocolate dessert with a coconut filling. I definitely enjoyed this dessert more than the avocado one. This was their seasonal dessert. It was far more decadent and I really hope it becomes permanent . The service was excellent this day as well.

Ambiance: Modern, sleek, colorful
Service:  great attentive waiters and waitresses.  Very friendly and easy to spark a convo on recommendations, jokes, or anything in particular.

Food: we had the crab nachos which were amazing.  Full flavor and plenty to go around for three.  The tuna tar tar is amazing.  Everything they serve up is well seasoned.  I had the skirt steak tacos.  While delicious, they only come in pairs.  They are pricey but well worth it.  Finally for the dessert, I had the blood orange flan which was too sweet for me.  My friend gave me a piece of the chocolate ice cream bar which was more my style.  Dark semi sweet chocolate that is not too sweet but enough to satisfy a savory meal.

Overall, a fantastic dinner.  I would come again but it is pricey.

Drinks:  spicy margaritas are fantastic.  They are not cheap but so worth it!  The costs can added fast if you lose track but they are really good.
Nice ambiance and delicious food! Service was great too! Will come back to try the fajita!

I met up with my Aunt, my cousin and her partner for dinner here and it was truly an amazing experience.

My aunt and I started at the bar with a spicy cucumber margarita and a variation on a Manhattan with tequila. The bartender recommended the por que no, si we tried that next and it was divine.

Once we sat for dinner we had the salsa sampler, a baked clam special, the steak fajitas and the crab nachos to share and all were amazing. 

The waiter gave perfect descriptions of everything and was charming.

Then....we ordered the Avocado dessert and the passion fruit dessert and we were blown away! 

Such an amazing meal! We will all come back here!

When I first walked I the area near the door was very loud and crowded.  Our party had not all arrived and they wouldn't seat us.  Bad start.  I went around the corner for a quick cocktail and when we arrived the remainder of our party arrived and they seated us.  From this point on the entire evening was a delight.  I thought about dropping a star for the initial interaction but decided against it since the rest of the evening was exceptional.  

Once we were seated we were presented with a selection of seven of the most exceptional dips I have ever enjoyed, all very interesting.  If the meal stopped there I would have been content.  The waiter, among the most knowledgeable I've run into including at some 3 Michelin star restaurants (a high bar).

Then he patiently described the tequilas in detail including the back story on many of the producers.  I won't share my absolute favorite small batch tequila since they only make 500 cases a year and I want to be able to get it! One of my friends and I decided we'd like to sample some of the tequilas and put ourselves in our waiters hands.  Wow.  I can only say wow.  Not the most expensive on the menu despite not giving him a limit which I always appreciate.

When we ordered he could detail every ingredient which I think is so important.  The food was interesting, certainly Mexican inspired but with a twist.  

And the bill was less than expected for this quality in NYC.

Not your typical Mexican restaurant. The drinks were great, strong and flavorful. The four bean salad was surprisingly the highlight of my meal. The chopped cabbage salad needed a bit more seasoning, the pastrami tacos was on the dry side and needed some sauce. The famed avocado dessert, although looks great, wasn't what I expected, I believe they used frozen avocados to make the whip as it had a slight citric acid taste. The flan and sherbet were great however.
Overrated. Overpriced. Service is disappointing.  Food is nothing impressive.  Will not recommend to anyone to this joint.

Overpriced garbage. It actually makes me quite mad. I was excited and tried multiple spots. For this spot I tried lunch a year ago and dessert this year. It tastes like bad grocery store food. And it is very very very expensive. And the staff is not nice. It is not a good experience. I have zero idea about the nice write ups about interesting food. If that did happen ever, it was a Long long long Ling time ago and if that exists, it doesn't exist for normal folks that visit today. There are many places in nyc doing interesting and delicious food. I tried here and they aren't doing it anymore.

Ordered guacamole and seven salsas for an appetizer. The steak tacos were great!  Ordered the saffron margarita which was very saffron forward. We saw the Brussels sprouts come out of the kitchen and definitely want to order those the next time.
Believe the other reviews. Overpriced for very average food. Hover over your table to force you out the door, like very awkwardly, even after you paid them so much. Would not recommend.

A friend and I had the prix fixe for lunch... $45.  Her cream soup did look good.  Lobster in my lobster salad was good, but the corn meal mixed with cream in the center was not very good.  I think it was about the "presentation" which was not very interesting.  The fish tacos were fine... fish was white and well done, but batter was too heavy for me.  I'm really not fond of fried food.  Only two tacos of medium size.  Dessert was sherbet, which was fine.  I only went here because my friend wanted to dine at a Michelin rated restaurant.   I could care less.  Presentation and creativity is not important to me.  I'd prefer more food.  The restaurant was crowded for lunch.  Clearly, lots of people don't feel the same way as me!

Medium- to low-quality Mexican food for the price of a sophisticated restaurant. Ordered prix-fixe lunch. Started with chowder, which was basically potatoes and water. Then the meat tacos, lower quality than your average fast food Mex fare. Even the sherbert (dessert) fell well below expectations. Paid $61 (with tip), which was probably $40 more than the food deserves. Major disappointment.

Now let me tell you. I was taken here to celebrate Sojvember aka my birthday month and baby hit the nail on the head. I stepped outside of my comfort zone a bit and loved the fact that I was rewarded with one of the best dinners I've had in a while.

The Christmas decor was beautiful, Usher was on the playlist, and the ambiance gave high scale Mexican restaurant. I already knew I was in for a good time. I'm not typically a tequila or mezcal kinda gal but "when in Rome", you feel me, & I'm so happy I went with it because the Pomegranate Margarita was fantastic. Strong yet subtly sweet. Two of those baby's & all was well in my world.

For starters we had the Guacamole with 7 Salsas. Neither of us eat guac (although it did look visually stunning) but the salsas were where the party was. I tried all 7 and the 5th & 6th towards the end (the spicier end) were my favorite. Asked for those badboys to go lol. I guarantee out of the 7, everyone will find at least one that they like. Then we had the fish tempura tacos. I'm typically not a Fish Taco person (you see a pattern here right lol) but babyyyy these tacos. Unfortunately, a lot of restaurants in NYC, forgot the basic art of seasoning their food, but this establishment did not. The fish itself with seasoned, the tempura batter was seasoned and the tartar sauce, and accompanying salsa was out of this world. Then, we had the Steak Fajitas. I don't typically order steak at a Mexican restaurant, but as soon as I sat down & made a comment to our waiter about how good a dish smelled, he let me know I was smelling that fajita. I knew it'd be seeing me. We asked for a medium cooked and got JUST that and again, SEASONED. I saw the flaky salt adorned on the steak as the smoke sizzled, and it's accompanied with a squeeze a fresh lime juice right on top. Nuff said. Lastly, we finished it out with the Apple Confit. You break a chocolate candy ball to be met with vanilla ice cream and caramel over a bed of apple almost gelatin bites. 

This place will be seeing me again. Whether I order the same thing or venture out again, I know for a fact it'll be great.

Empellon was suggested as a good spot for a work lunch, and it is! 

I was initially intimidated by the prix fixe menu because of the amount of food, but you are able to order a la carte. We started with the guacamole that comes with five different salsas - I had never mixed and experimented with so many salsas but they really do allow you to put your own twist on the guacamole.

I ordered the steak tacos which were solid. The tortillas were thinner and far more delicate than I expected - they fell apart before I even picked them up so ended up having to eat them with a knife and fork. (gasp!)

Reservations are a must as it gets packed for lunch. We had an early reservation at 11:30a and, as I was leaving at around 12:30, the restaurant was 100% full. The restaurant has a relatively spacious feel given that it is quite compact (probably because of the high ceilings). There are a limited number of outdoor tables.

We had a reservation for 8 pm. It was busy but we were sat right away. The food and drinks came out super quick, wait staff was attentive and great, the food and drinks were DELICIOUS. Chips and salsa combo was definitely different but everyone enjoyed it. Will be back!
They have the best fish tacos I've ever had - great margaritas and terrific service - I'm here weekly
Great food and service and I'd give 5 star rating in those categories. A bit noisy so for ambience so it's 3 star from me. Overall I recommend highly.

I went to a pre-show dinner at Empellon with my husband and another couple a week or so ago, and it was a disappointment. 

We shared: guacamole with seven salsas; crab nachos with sea urchin "queso"; roasted shishito peppers with lime vinaigrette; carrots with coconut crema and spicy coriander oil; lobster tacos with potatoes and dark chile paste; ground dry aged beef picadillo with a crunchy taco shell and Vermont cheddar blend; and their classic dessert - the avocado that isn't an avocado (lime raspado and eucalyptus yogurt). A few of the things we ordered were fine, but none were great and some weren't very good at all. The seven salsas that came with the guacamole - some of them were too sweet for me, which was strange. The crab nachos were a total disappointment, especially because it was over $30; they were dry and bland and mostly just dry chips and crab that seemed dried out with a tasteless "queso." The carrots were undercooked, which I would be okay with if they weren't also underseasoned and bland. The tacos were okay - nothing to write home about, but better than most of the dishes we had. I would say the only things I enjoyed and would consider ordering again were the shishito peppers and the avocado. I also ordered the pumpkin seed cappelletti with achiote and honey nut squash juice which I was really looking forward to, but it never arrived, so I just told them to make sure it wasn't on the bill.

The service was also pretty bad. Our server barely spoke to us. I had to start waving to get his attention because he wasn't stopping by to check on us even though they weren't busy (I need to ask for more chips, to add something to our order, and to ask for our check since we were going to a show and he hadn't come by in so long he didn't know we hadn't received our last dish). They also brought me the wrong wine (easily corrected) and forgot one of our dishes. But our server was not just helpful or friendly. 

The space is nice, and the location was convenient for a show after dinner. But that's really all I can say that was positive about our meal. I didn't enjoy the food or the service, and I would not return based on this experience. I can't think of a more disappointing meal this year, which was all the more disappointing given the number on the bill.

Little bit expensive, but that's the price for a great location. Guac was great and 7 salsas were interesting as well. Tacos were a bit small but good quality. Restaurant was pretty large and loud, which was good. Would recommend if looking for decent Mexican food near west village.

I came here for a company event. Our manager had chosen the place for a team dinner outing. We had ordered a bunch of different appetizers that was perfect for our group size so that I didn't have to think about what to order. Everything tasted amazing and no matter how full we were we still had extra room for dessert, an avocado shaped key lime pie. The service was just as great, we were checked in on regular basis and our water was always full. Can't wait to come back.

this place was okay. I was kind of disappointed. The service was not bad, but it was pretty sparse and as soon as we took a pause from our meals they came and took every single plate, before all the people eating were done, and continued to do that with our drinks/apps throughout the meal. It felt like we were being rushed a lot. The food was mediocre, I thought. My friend got the shrimp tacos and liked it, but the chicken tacos and the quesadilla were just okay. The salsa flight was honestly the best part, delicious and fun to try!

It's surprising when restaurants nail the food and then get everything else wrong. I feel this warrants some feedback.

The food was 5star and the experience was 1star. 

If you go here make sure you sit upstairs because downstairs is just too noisy. An overwhelming number of men in suits just standing around cursing and drinking. Bumping into your table.  And this was on Wednesday, can't imagine another day of the week. Is it always like this or was there a private event? 

Because it's so noisy why use giant Cheesecake Factory sized tables downstairs? Creates less space and there is no chance you can talk to the person across from you without yelling. I feel using small tables downstairs will help a lot. There was a large party sitting next to us and you can see they could only talk to the people seated adjacent to them. They completely gave up on trying to talk across the table. 

The art is strange. We were sitting next to a sculpture of a rooster with tits laying in a kinda sexual pose. I don't mind the sculpture but it's an odd choice for a restaurant. Anyways it gave us a laugh so maybe it's a good thing. 

And finally our server lectured me about ordering a drink from someone who was not him, and because I did that, he has no idea where my drink is and it may never show up. Bizarre to get this lecture at a fine dining restaurant. But damn the drink was so good. 

Again I should emphasize the food and drinks were 5star 
 and I'm sure the upstairs experience is more pleasant. They need to sort out downstairs if they plan to sit people there for dinner. I will go back and sit upstairs next time. 

#roosterwithtits
Spectacular food and service. The fish with curry sauce is something I keep thinking about! And don't miss the "avocado" ice cream!

Finally came to the this location. Our server was excellent. The cocktails was excellent, and it was hard to pick a favorite. I really need to say the pumpkin pasta special is absolutely amazing and surprisingly flavorful. I would definitely return.

Amazing!! Hugo - makes u-go crazy for the drinks! The food is fresh and new wave nothing like it. The Avocado totally messes with you mind what you see is NOT what you get it's better - need to get here and soon. Reservations are hot so do it! Love this place / LAD

The spicy cucumber margarita, guacamole & seven salsas, maitake tacos, sweet potatoes and fish tacos are delicious! The avocado and mahleb gelee desserts are mind blowing-incredible! Andres gave above and beyond service.

TLDR; if you're feeling like a normal quick lunch isn't enough, come here and have some absolutely delicious and light dishes. 

Came here for lunch and did the prix fixe menu. 

- Chopped cabbage salad
- tomato salad
- Maitake mushroom tacos
- pastrami tacos
- sour cherry flan
- chocolate ice cream sandwich
- Brussels sprouts
- spicy cucumber margarita

Standouts we're the Pastrami Tacos, Brussels sprouts, and the chopped cabbage salad. Spicy marg was solid too, my first one!

Definitely the best high end Mexican in Manhattan.   A bit pricy, but well worth it. The saffron margaritas are worth a visit by themselves, but the food is consistently good across the board. Be sure to save room for dessert.

5-star service and delicious food. The only thing keeping me from giving it 5 stars is the value proposition. I know it's midtown and things are pricier these days, but when my friend and I saw the size of our seared halibut (priced at around $39), we both wanted to know where the rest of it was. My piece of fish was about an inch by four inches - a sliver of a filet. His was a tad larger but not by much. We both enjoyed the coconut-basil broth, and the fish was perfectly cooked. But we had to order a third entree (the mushroom tacos) in order to feel full. And this was after having three appetizers: the chips and guac with all the salsas (also very good), the smoked cod (very tasty but tiny little bites) and the queso fundido. The cocktails were the one thing that seemed to pair flavor and value. I had their version of a gin martini, which was nuanced and delicious, as well as the espresso martini. Two well balanced drinks that, thankfully, weren't as tiny as the entrees.

Don't waste your time. I've been to their taco location, which is much better but for the price skip this spot. The food is average and the price is HIGH. They have good cocktails but honestly not worth the almost 20 dollar price tag. I know that can be normal for NYC but it's not worth it at this spot. Vibes are bland, midtown location with nothing else nearby, just a snooze all around.

We had a very bad experience with this restaurant because we called the restaurant in advance and asked what time they close since we want to come for dinner. They said they have the last seating at 10 pm for food so we arrived at 9.30! Upon arrival the host consulted with the kitchen before sitting us and then told us the kitchen is closed! What is this? On their website it says they close at 10pm, why you guys provide the false info on your website and on the phone when in reality you are just lazy  and ready to lose customers! I will tell all my friends how unprofessional the service is! Very bad!

This was a great spot for a work lunch. 

Fish tacos were really good, salsas and chips were great, and the tuna was also fantastic. My personal favorite was the rhubarb dessert which is truly outstanding. 

Service and drinks were fine. It's a good setup and convenient location for business lunches, and the food comes out pretty fast so that works well also. I'll likely come here again for future meetings.
Great happy hour stop! Much needed after exploring the village. Large tequila selection!

Having lived in San Diego for 4 years, it's difficult to get Mexican food anywhere else. Decided to give Empellon a try and it was a pleasant surprise! Granted, it's definitely given a more "modern" touch here and dishes are crafted with the utmost precision. 

It seemed everyone had started with the seven salsa appetizer, and it was highly recommended, so we decided to go for that one too. The seven salsas are arranged so that the spice levels increase as you keep going. My favourite was the first one: a cashew cream that was so creamy, with a hint of smokeyness to it. This with the guac together was perfection! The chips were also refilled and we just couldn't stop eating them and adding all the different sauces to it. I'd recommend taking it slow with the chips, especially since we had lots of food coming and were a bit full from the chips! 

For others, we got the jumbo prawn fajitas, fish tacos, and an asparagus special of the evening. The white asparagus, as explained to us, was grown completely in the darkness (no photosynthesis, no chlorophyll). The texture was really great, and was a light dish in comparison to the heavier foods that were to come. Fish tacos were great as you'd expect, though I personally added a few more sauces from our appetizer onto it for just a little more "zing." We were getting quite full at this point, but each decided to try a fajita - six pieces of tortilla come with it, and you make it yourself. The juices of the dish were so well blended in, but we weren't expecting it to be quite spicy! I really did like that though, and brought the rest home since we were full, but it was even better the next day given that the flavour had all soaked in at this point. 

For dessert, we just had to try the avocado ice cream. The presentation is flawless - it really looks like an avocado even in real life when it's in front of you. I couldn't really tell what the flavour was really, just that it was a mousse like texture and melted instantly. The lemon ice cream shavings accompanying it were a great touch to balance out the milder avocado.

I rarely have poor dining experiences, and this was a memorable one. The bartender was not a ppl person (wrong industry, guy). The seven salsas is cute, but $18 guacamole was the size of half an avocado smashed. I'll take the taco truck, pls.

author.name: Megan T.
author.location: Upper West Side, New York, NY

reviews.review: The service was great however this place is definitely NOT for everyone. If you like bland, unseasoned, uncooked food then this place is perfect for you. If you prefer REAL Mexican food then go to an authentic Mexican restaurant.

BLOWN AWAY by this restaurant!!! My drinks were perfection and the seven salsas were PHENOMENAL. I had several other appetizers and entrees and everything was like a work of art. Our server had some fabulous recommendations. Beautiful atmosphere. Highly recommended!
Wonderful, delicious refined Mexican cuisine.  Dishes you know, but executed to perfection and some fun twists too.  Pastrami tacos anyone?  Yea, they were awesome, as was everything.
Excellent food, especially the pastrami and lobster tacos. Will be back again and again. The service is generally good and the atmosphere is very causal.

They were closed for a while due to covid so this was my first time being back since they re-opened. It was just as good as I remembered!! It wasn't super busy which was nice - wasn't too loud and atmosphere was warm and welcoming. Got great seating. I ordered the crab nachos which were to die for - full of flavor, I couldn't stop eating them! Entrees we're great per usual - got an order of tacos and so did my boyfriend so we shared both orders which was the perfect amount of food. For dessert we always get the ice cream sandwiches though one of the employees recommended this avocado dessert... he was rly pushing it on us so I was hesitant but decided to get it anyways. It was DELICIOUS! Believe it or not - that is not a real avocado! It tastes just like key lime pie and the white stuff around it tasted like a bougie dip and dots haha overall great experience AGAIN. 10/10 recommend.

Didn't have the best experience unfortunately. We came during restaurant week but ended up not doing the restaurant week pre-fixe. 
Crab uni nachos sounded compelling but didn't impress us. All NYC restaurants are pricey but this place really didn't seem worth the cost at all. Cocktails were good! Service was extremely hands on. Would not go back.

I received a voicemail yesterday asking to confirm my reservation for 2:30 this afternoon, by the time I listened to the voicemail it was late in the evening and I was unable to call you back. Without receiving word from me, it appears that my reservation was canceled. I was unaware of the cancellation until I arrived at 2:30 today. The restaurant was supposed to be open until 3 PM, but the door was locked and I was ignored by the staff.

Thankfully I was able to find alternate arrangements around the corner at Nerai for my business meeting, but I just wanted to provide a review to inform others of my experience. In the future, I would recommend that you do not cancel reservations made before you receive word from the individual who made them.

Empellon is the "fine dining" restaurant of the Alex Stupak Empellon mini-empire. While the food and service are certainly more upscale than his downtown establishments, the flavors are every bit as bold and creative. As always with Stupak the quesos, salsas and tacos are the stars of the show. While all the cocktails are good, stick to the margaritas. By the way, Alex Stupak is a dessert chef by training so leave room for dessert.

My first time here & totally wowed by the food, the service, drinks & dessert (do not leave here without the apple confit)!  
Lobster tacos & fish tacos were incredible.

Came for dinner with a friend and had a great experience. We ordered:

+ Mother of dragons cocktail
+ Spicy cucumber margarita 
+ The safe word cocktail
+ Pomegranate margarita
+ Guacamole
+ Tuna tartare 
+ Fish tempura tacos
+ Maitake mushroom tacos
+ Skirt steak
+ Avocado dessert

The highlights were the guac, skirt steak and famed avocado dessert (so wild). They also gave us a complimentary apple peel sorbet infused with canela and hibiscus, which was awesome.

Order the desserts, especially "avocado."
Crab uni nacho was unsatisfactory. There's hardly any uni or uni flavor in the dish. 
Pastrami tacos were just ok.
Rib steak fajita was good. Maybe ask them not to squeeze lime for you. 
The wine list could be more fun. Ordered a Bordeaux, but it'll be nice to see a more varied Rosé (darker ones for the winter?) list. 
Staffs were friendly, but one of the waiters (or floor manager) in suits upstairs was pushing to order more dishes. I'm used to that kind of sales style, but it's distracting when I want to enjoy a meal with friends.

We were a group of five for dinner last night with 8:30 reservations, greeted warmly and seated immediately in this lovely upscale Mexican restaurant. It was busy, pretty full with a mostly business crowd. We had great service and a delicious meal followed by some of the most beautiful, delicious and unique desserts ever. However, at the end of our meal, just after our server had taken our credit cards to run the check, the manager of the restaurant appeared at our table to inform us that we needed to wrap up our evening and leave because the restaurant was closing. It was nearing 11:00, we had given the server our check and just needed to sign the checks. We had not a lingered over drinks or coffee and had not in any way caused any disturbance. Several servers saw the incident and all were very apologetic and embarrassed. The manager came back over and defended his position, not apologizing for his behavior. None in our group of seasoned travelers and diners had ever experienced such behavior in a fine dining venue.

Another wonderful experience with delicious guacamole and sauces, very good skirt steak and pasta and yummy margaritas. The service is sofantastic, attentive, experienced  and accommodating that we can't wait to return. THANK YOU STEVEN for being such a warm, knowledgeable and incredible foodie and for your great recommendations and impeccable service.

Great for business lunches. The environment is clean and modern. Basically the whole lunch menu is part of pre fixe but you can still order individual items in there a la carte. The limited menu also means food prep can be faster - they were quick in bringing out dishes. I wish they would give us more time to finish things tho
I'm open to coming for lunch myself too. 

-

We ordered crab nachoes and tuna tartar to start and share. Both were pretty big. 
Tuna tartar - it was seasoned such that it didn't feel like I was eating tartar, bit spicy and savory. I typically am not a fan of these things, but I liked this. The pumpkin seeds on top were powdered so it didn't add much texture. They gave a lot. An area of improvement might be to provide a medium to eat along with the tuna. It's still good as is. 
Crab nachoes - again large portions. I like the savoriness of this but I wonder if it'll be too much if I get to eat more. If I had to choose out of the two I feel like the tuna is more special. 

Appetizers arrived soon after the shared plates. Tolerable but prefer more time to get to them. 
I got carrots. Sometimes I'm amused by their names because I have no idea what it means. I thought the carrots are stewed or something but turns out it's a cold salad. The creme and seasoning made this hearty despite the temperature. 
The cauliflower soup is a hot option. 

Main I got steak taco. They're soft corn tacos. It was torn the moment I picked it up, so I resorted to using fork to eat this. 
Otherwise the steak was good, no tendons, no fatty bits. 

Dessert 
The sorbet is cute how it comes in one big disk with all three flavors intertwined. 
Avocado - I came here practically solely for this. It's definitely very pretty. They even have the details like the indent for the top of the avocado where the stem connects. Too bad they didn't use a raisin or seed or chocolate or cookie to replicate that too. The actual avocado is some mousse like item. The menu mentioned something like yogurt. There's not too much gelatin in this where it'd taste stiff and plastic - good balance. Otherwise I can't point a finger at the exact flavor of the avocado. The plating had lime sorbet which melts as you scoop it (amused me) and it gave good juiciness to the otherwise monotonous avocado. It would be nice to add some texture (e.g. coconut or Graham cracker crumbs) but that might affect the visual of the sorbet. Hidden within the sorbet is a spoonful of cream that was used to secure the avocado in the middle of the plate.
Tastewise the avocado is not that special, but adding in the visual aspect it is definitely worth trying. 

-

Pre fixe alone is a bit not enough food but very good for the price $39. I think one shareable is good addition for two ppl.

Besides rushing us the food, my only other complaint here is the physical space between the tables. I gave up on the idea of social distancing, but the spacing is so tight I have difficulty getting in and out of my seat on the bench side.

The food at Empellon is undoubtedly some of the best elevated Mexican food this country has to offer. But beyond the food, i cannot speak highly enough about the service. The food is as full of personality, charm, and elegance as the the waitstaff themselves. Our server, Allan was a total delight. Bubbly, genuine, and full of personality--unlike the dry, sterile service you so often experience at similarly upscale establishments such as this one. Such a refreshing surprise for midtown dining!
Great menu and excellent food. My go to place lunch and dinner. I would recommend the Steak Tacos.

Everything about my experience here was perfect. I took my girlfriend here for a birthday lunch, and the food and service was impeccable. Gabriel took excellent care of us, explained every dish in such great detail and he's a big reason I'd come back to this location! The famous avocado dessert was amazing, both in flavor and presentation - you'd be hard pressed to find someone who doesn't think it's just a regular avocado at first, or even second glance. Strongly recommended.

Looking forward to my next visit!

This place is amazing! Gabriel took fantastic care of us. The guacamole and salsa sampler were so good. And the queso tasted out of this world. The margaritas were amazing as well. Perfect spot for lunch.

author.name: Dahlia F.
author.location: Salt Lake City, Salt Lake City, UT

reviews.review: I actually really like this place. Great tacos and I'm obsessed with their chorizo cheese appetizer!

Empellón you are absolutely amazing, I had a lovely experience here today. Overall, great atmosphere, ambiance, cleanliness and customer service. Highly impressed with their menu, lots of great options, Pastrami Tacos was absolutely magnificent. The staff members are all extremely nice and helpful. Empellón = Amazing.

It was my first visit to Empellon, and will definitely not be my last.  The atmosphere was grown and stylish without being fussy. The service was exceptional, and the short rib confit was so good --so tender.  The pastrami tacos were a wonderful bite as well. The only downside is that they don't deliver to me in Cincinnati...yet.

Terrific lunch last week.  Took two clients, and they were huge fans.  7 salsas were great - 2nd hottest was particularly tasty.  Had some fish tacos - fresh fish, perfect tortillas.  Dessert ice cream sandwiches looked good, but I just watched my partners chow them down.

Side note on post-meal service - like a dummy, I forgot to take my receipt. Empellon was super cool about sending me an itemized bill 3 days after I called about it.

Would definitely return!

Ode To The Short Rib Confit
So tender, so delicious. 
With a pairing of tortilla and jalapeños galore, 
my friend saw my mouth watering so he gave me more
The Short Rib Confit is the way to go
I think about it all the time, I miss it so. 

The guac game was a delight
with a perfect salsa flight

The only thing that missed its mark
was the chocolate sampling dessert
we ordered it on a lark
but, well, next time we'd avert

The avocado yogurt on the other hand
now that was a treat
to make it look SO MUCH LIKE AN AVOCADO
now that is a feat

Thank you, Empellón, 
we'll be back for you soon
please fix the chocolate
and we'll surely swoon!

The margaritas were good and physical space is nice, that is where the positive aspect of this review ends.
The whole dining experience  felt rushed and chaotic. We got our apps and it took forever for the guacamole to come out. Not long after the guacamole came out the entrees did, which we then sent back. Once our entrees returned I found my steak to be cold. At this point I had given up and ate my cold steak and it didn't taste bad but was still cold.
Then we ordered coffee and after dinner drinks, 1 drink came out 10 minutes before the other 3 coffees which just comes off as unorganized. We had to ask wherE the coffees were instead of us being told that they were coming and the staff seemed irritated at our questions.
All in it was a lackluster and disappointing experience!

I love the dessert and I luv the Mexican flavor. 
The food is seasoned well and still keeps the moisture in it.

The avocado dessert is a real surprise! It's creamy but not too rich cuz it has the sour ice around. Recommend it to everyone! 

Comparatively, it's easy to reserve a seat here, just plan a day ahead. Luv the Mexican cuisine, will be back soon!

I really like almost everything about this place. The haute cuisine Mexican/seafood is delicious. Especially the cabbage salad and fish tacos. The desserts are crazy creative. Try the mousse/flan made to look like an avocado but taste like key lime!   The service is brisk but solicitous. It can get busy but they handle it fairly well. It is noisy but not unbearable. There are several locations in Manhattan. This is for the Madison Ave location

I've been to Empellón twice now and both times have thought the food was great. That being said, when I am craving cheesy, saucy Mexican food is not when I go to Empellón. The food here is definitely more upscale and so are the prices.

- Queso Fundido: The fundido is topped with steak tartare which might seem amazing to some people, just not to me. I prefer more traditional fundido where the cheese is blistery and a little crispy. The cheese here is more saucy and creamy, and I learned I do not like raw beef, particularly on top of hot dishes.

- BLT Tacos: The BLT tacos were super fun! The bacon is thick cut and there are three to an order so I prefer to share the tacos and get a few types.

- The guacamole and salsas: I love how they serve seven different salsas, all very colorful and ranging from sweet and creamy to extremely spicy. My favorite is the one made from cashews - I put it on everything!

- Avocado: The infamous avocado which is actually made of a thick key lime cream and served on top a bed of lemon shaved ice that is meant to look like salt. This dish is fun and delicious - the best combo!

Overall, the food is great with unique and exciting dishes you won't have seen anywhere else! When I am in the mood for upscale food with the flavors of Mexican food, I go here!

Wanted a Mexican night out with friends and Empellon did not disappoint! Was able to easily get a reservation for 4 on a Saturday night and we were seated promptly when we arrived at the restaurant. The scene was lively, lots of people in groups of friends, a fun looking communal table down the centre of the restaurant. Started off with guacamole and their house made chips which were delicious! Everyone ordered tacos. I personally had the Brussels sprouts tacos (delicious!) and the fish tempura (also delicious, on the spicier side). Other things ordered at the table were the sweet potatoes flautas, skirt steak tacos and chicken tacos, and the Saturday night special scallops taco. We all loved our food and I would definitely return!

Nice atmosphere and decor. Upscale feel. Service was very good. A very sharp looking staff. 

The menu for dinner was limited and focused on seafood.  The ingredients were highlighted in a way the lead to expectations of complex flavors... unfortunately for me it did not deliver those flavors.  With the exception of one dish (short ribs) all tasted of one note/one ingredient or one seasoning.

I've only been to Empellon once, but thought the food was pretty unique. This is a vegetarian review and I haven't tried any of the tacos or meat-based mains. 

I shared the guacamole with seven salsas and ordered the pumpkin seed cappelletti. I loved the concept where you could pair different salsas with the chips and guac since the salsas have all sorts of flavor profiles and range from non-spicy to decently spicy. I thought the pumpkin seed cappelletti, although I haven't tried anything like it previously, was overall too salty. I appreciate that there was at least one vegetarian option in every category (tacos, mains, starters, etc.)

I recognize that Empellon is meant to have a cool ambiance with the dim lighting, but main dining area was so loud that it was difficult to have a conversation. Although I won't be frequenting, I think Empellon would be worth a try.

Probably too much emphasis on presentation and ambience than foods.  Every dish tempted me to take a picture.  Then I don't really remember which one impressed me on flavors.

We had two bottles: white and red. They were good, but priced at $90.

Not that I am a New Yorker, but I would recommend sticking to an ethnic focus (Mexican?) and impress customers with uniqueness in flavors.

this by far the worst restaurant i've ever attended, food options are extremely limited and the food options that they are serving is inedible, i had the pastrami tacos and the bread of the taco tasted like it was straight out of a dish washer... i will never come back to this place and if i had the option of zero stars i would choose it. on top of all of this they don't serve CHICKEN during dinner... i wouldn't recommend this restaurant to my worst e

came here for a few drinks the other night. they have a bouncer and stamp you at the door which I felt was a bit excessive for trying to grab a margarita... 

the drinks themselves were good though they felt a little weak. our bartender was very helpful and nice and did accommodate our request to make them spicier after we first tried them. 

come here if you want a decent drink and good vibe- dont if you care about the craft of your drink or want to get drunk

I went here to celebrate a friends birthday and the food was very good, but in my opinion very overpriced. We got the crab nachos for the table which were delicious and had a good amount of crab meat on them. For entree I got the short rib which was fantastic. It was a nice change from the way short rib is usually prepared and had such a fresh flavor. My friend got the lamb which was cooked perfectly and the sauce was delicious. Overall the food was great, the ambiance was perfect for a date night or gathering of close friends, just too expensive to go back as frequently as I would like to.

MOST AMAZING FOOD IVE EVER HAD IN MY WHOLE LIFE. The waiter was super sweet and the food came quickly. I never review food but this truly was the most amazing food I've ever had. It was flavorful and each bite was like heaven.
